title: Review: Balanced equations and reacting masses; Oxidation states and naming; Radioactivity and nuclear equations (Eduqas)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RX02#t3 term and clue written for the game; RX02#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t4 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM07#N.12a, NU01#N.7, RX02#N.4a, AM07#N.4a, NU01#N.14, RX02#N.10, AM07#N.6a, NU01#N.4, RX02#N.8, AM07#N.14, NU01#N.13. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Metal hydride
items.clue: Compound such as NaH or CaH₂ in which H is −1.

items.label: Peroxide
items.clue: Compound such as H₂O₂ or Na₂O₂ in which O is −1.

items.label: Precipitate
items.clue: A solid formed when two solutions react, e.g. AgCl from Ag⁺ and Cl⁻.

items.label: State symbols
items.clue: The labels (s), (l), (g) and (aq) written after each species in an equation.

questions.stem: Iron is produced by reducing iron(III) oxide with carbon monoxide: Fe₂O₃(s) + 3CO(g) → 2Fe(s) + 3CO₂(g). What is the maximum mass of iron that can be produced from 40.0 g of iron(III) oxide? (Ar: O 16.0, Fe 55.8)
A beam containing α, β⁻ and γ radiation passes between two oppositely charged parallel plates. Which statement describes the β⁻ radiation?

options.text: It bends towards the positive plate, by more than the α radiation bends
It bends towards the negative plate, by more than the α radiation bends
It bends towards the positive plate, by less than the α radiation bends
It passes straight through between the plates without bending at all

questions.explanation: Negative, so attracted to the positive plate; very light, so deflected much more than α.

questions.stem: What are the oxidation numbers of hydrogen in sodium hydride, NaH, and of oxygen in sodium peroxide, Na₂O₂?
questions.explanation: In NaH, Na is +1, so H is −1 (the hydride ion). In Na₂O₂, 2(+1) + 2x = 0, so O is −1 (the peroxide ion, O₂²⁻).

questions.stem: Aluminium burns in oxygen to form aluminium oxide. Which equation for this reaction is correctly balanced?
questions.explanation: Al₂O₃ and O₂ are the right formulae. 3O₂ gives 6 O = 2Al₂O₃, which needs 4Al. 4 Al and 6 O each side.

questions.stem: Phosphorus-32 (t½ = 14.3 days) is used to label DNA in biochemical analysis. A sample's count rate (corrected for background) falls from 1600 to 100 counts per minute. How long did this take?
Chlorine is −1 in the chloride ion, Cl⁻, but +1 in the hypochlorite ion, ClO⁻ (in bleach). Which explains the +1?

options.text: The chlorine atom in ClO⁻ has lost a proton to the oxygen atom, leaving chlorine with a +1 charge.
Oxygen always has the oxidation number −1 in an ion with one negative charge.
Oxygen is more electronegative than chlorine, so it is assigned the shared electrons in the Cl–O bond.
The chlorine atom in ClO⁻ carries a real charge of +1, as in a Cl⁺ ion.

questions.explanation: O takes both shared electrons and is −2; the total must be −1, so x + (−2) = −1 and Cl is +1. In Cl⁻, chlorine holds an extra electron: −1.

questions.stem: Magnesium ribbon fizzes and dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid. Which is the ionic equation for the reaction?
questions.explanation: Cl⁻ is a spectator. 1 Mg and 2 H each side; charge 2+ each side.

questions.stem: Copper-64 is used in medical imaging. One way it decays is: ⁶⁴₂₉Cu → ⁶⁴₂₈Ni + X. What is X?
questions.explanation: A: 64 = 64 + 0. Z: 29 = 28 + 1. A positron. (Electron capture also makes Ni-64, but its electron is on the left.)
2(+1) + 2x + 7(−2) = 0 gives 2x = +12, so each Cr is +6. The numeral is per atom.

questions.stem: A strip of magnesium burns brightly in air and leaves white magnesium oxide: 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s). What mass of MgO forms from 2.43 g of Mg? (Ar: O 16.0, Mg 24.3)
A hospital needs a radioisotope to inject into a patient so that a camera outside the body can image the kidneys. Which isotope is most suitable?

options.text: An α emitter with a half-life of 6 hours
A γ emitter with a half-life of 6 hours
A γ emitter with a half-life of 5 years
A β⁻ emitter with a half-life of 8 days

questions.explanation: γ rays pass out of the body to the camera, and the short half-life keeps the patient's dose low.
